subject: Sourcing path evaluation: PO vs card & marketplace interest
messages:
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Jill Torres <jill.torres@procurenow.com>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.com>, Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Sourcing path evaluation: PO vs card & marketplace interest

Hi Jill — thanks again for the time earlier. Quick post-call recap and a few clarifying asks so our teams can align on the commercial path and procurement readiness. I’ve attached a short procurement checklist and a draft mutual action plan for review.

Recap (what I heard)
- Procurement requires vendor registration + completed W-9 and proof of insurance for any new vendor.
- AP typically processes via PO for recurring contracts; card use is allowed for one-off or pilot purchases but is restricted by single-transaction and monthly limits.
- There is internal interest in buying via AWS Marketplace to centralize billing and entitlements.

Open questions for your team
1) Can you confirm the approximate card spend threshold that forces PO-only routing? (You mentioned $10k+, want exact cutoff.)
2) For pilots, would Procurement accept a temporary card-based purchase under $15k/month with a short-term invoice and then convert to PO if we expand?
3) Is marketplace procurement mandatory for all teams or only for cloud services? If mandatory, what intake/forms are required from our side to initiate Marketplace listing?
4) Any vendor onboarding forms beyond W-9 and COI (certificate of insurance)?

Next steps proposed
- We’ll circulate the draft mutual action plan and a PO template (Marissa).
- If card pilot is acceptable, Naomi will prepare a pilot invoice option and note the processing fee implications.
- Mateo to coordinate marketplace intake timeline with your procurement lead.

Attachments: redwood-procurement-checklist.pdf (summary of forms we typically provide), mutual-action-plan-draft.xlsx

Thanks — quick replies to the 4 questions above will help us scope the pilot and go/no-go timelines.

—

Subject: Re: Sourcing path evaluation: PO vs card & marketplace interest

Mateo — great recap, and appreciate the checklist. A few clarifications from Procurement: 

- Card threshold: our policy routes anything over $12,500 to AP review and generally requires a PO for recurring commitments above $10k/month. One-off pilot purchases under $12,500 can use corporate card but need approval from the line manager + AP notification.
- Pilots: we can do a card-based pilot if total committed spend stays under $12,500 and you include a note that card-processing fees will be absorbed by the vendor or billed separately (our standard).
- Marketplace: AWS Marketplace is our preferred route for SaaS that integrates with cloud entitlements — it shortens procurement by ~2 weeks because contracts are standardized. However, not every business unit requires Marketplace; the security/compliance team mandates Marketplace only for services that require entitlements tied to cloud accounts.
- Onboarding docs: W-9 is mandatory; COI typically requested for >$25k ARR or where professional services are involved. We also require a primary contact for invoice disputes and a remittance address (ACH preferred).

I’ll introduce our AP lead if you want to discuss PO templates and net terms. We’re open to a card-based pilot for the first 30–60 days under the thresholds above.

—
Jill Torres
Senior Procurement Manager | ProcureNow
jill.torres@procurenow.com | +1 (212) 555-0102

Team — quick internal note after Jill’s reply:
- The $12.5k card cap lines up with what we’ve seen at similar mid-market customers. For pilots, recommend we propose a capped monthly invoice (<= $12k) payable by card, with a clause that converts to PO/N30 on expansion. That removes friction for them and keeps our ops tidy.
- Finance: we should disclose who absorbs card processing fees. Typical play: vendor absorbs fees for the first 60 days or we split for trials over $5k. Naomi, can you draft two variants (vendor-absorbed fees vs split) for legal review?
- Marketplace: if ProcureNow signals preference for AWS Marketplace, flag Legal and Cloud Partnerships early — marketplace lead time (listing + procurement ops) is ~3–4 weeks. If they require Marketplace for entitlement reasons, that will accelerate legal intake.

I’ll add a short note to the mutual action plan with these options.

—
